front: What are the three parts of the Golden Triangle?
back: Sport; Media; Sponsorship
group: Golden triangle

front: What is commercialisation?
back: The process of attempting to gain money from an activity, e.g. sport
group: Golden triangle

front: What is sponsorship?
back: When a company pays for its products to be publicly displayed or advertised, usually to increase sales
group: Golden triangle

front: What is media?
back: An organised means of communication by which large numbers of different people can be reached quickly
group: Golden triangle

front: What are the characteristics of commercial sport?
back: Professional sport with high quality and skill levels; Sponsorship and business go hand in hand; Sport is mass entertainment; Events are structured to fit relatively short viewing times; Contracts involve merchandise sales and television rights; Athletes become commodities through product endorsement; Wide media coverage focuses on visually appealing, high-quality sports with simple rules and close competition
group: Golden triangle

front: What are the effects of commercialisation on professional performers?
back: Receive high incomes from participation and endorsements, providing financial security and allowing full-time training; Paid for success so winning becomes important; Can be pressured to compete when injured; Must specialise and dedicate themselves to one sport; Become entertainers and household names; Controlled by sponsors, become public commodities and lose privacy
group: Golden triangle

front: What are the effects of commercialisation on sport?
back: Rules and scoring systems have changed to speed up play and reduce boredom (e.g. multi-ball in football, rally scoring in badminton); Breaks allow sponsors to advertise; Competition formats have changed (e.g. Twenty20 cricket); Women's sport receives less media coverage, reducing funding, participation and role models; Increased technology has created a more personal viewing experience
group: Golden triangle

front: Why do companies invest in sport?
back: Increased sales, publicity and profit; Greater brand awareness and brand value; Association with excellence at the highest level of sport; Association with a healthy image; Corporate hospitality opportunities; Tax relief; Improved company morale through association with sporting success
group: Golden triangle

front: What is the role of the media in sport?
back: The media includes newspapers, radio, the internet, television and social media; Buying and selling TV broadcasting rights is important because sport has become global; Globalisation links nations through improved communication and travel
group: Golden triangle

front: What is globalisation and what is one negative of it?
back: The increasing connection of nations through communication and travel; Seen through global sponsorship (e.g. Coca-Cola), international player recruitment and the spread of sports to new countries (e.g. 1994 FIFA World Cup in the USA); A negative is increased pressure on athletes, which may encourage the use of illegal performance-enhancing substances
group: Golden triangle

front: What is the impact of social media on sport?
back: Social media consists of online apps and websites where users share content and interact; It has changed the behaviour of performers and fans at all levels; Younger generations increasingly use platforms such as Twitter and Facebook to keep up to date with sport instead of television or national news websites
group: Golden triangle

front: What is the amateur code?
back: Stresses that sport should be played for the love of it

front: What is the professional code?
back: Places more emphasis on winning, prizes and money

front: What were some characteristics of amateurism in the late 19th century?
back: Manliness and physical endeavour; Appreciating the value of mind and health; Appreciating the value of rule-regulated activity; High moral integrity

front: What were some characteristics of the gentleman amateur?
back: Being a respected member of society; Participation was character-building and training was frowned upon; Played sport to a high moral code; Referees were deemed unnecessary as they believed they could govern themselves

front: What were some positive impacts of amateurism?
back: Elite sport was run by the middle and upper classes; Code of amateurism; Code of ethics; Belonging to the social elite; Participation in sport was more important than winning; The middle class admired the values of the upper class

front: What increased as sport became more popular and what did the working class have more of?

front: What background did professionals come from?

front: What were the positive impacts of 19th-century professionalism on sport development?

front: What are some key features of early 20th-century amateurs?

front: What are some features of modern-day professionalism?

back: The movement from rural to urban environments

front: What were some characteristics of the modern-day development of association football?
back: Urbanisation leading to more spectators and specialist facilities; More disposable income through higher wages and increased ticket sales; Improved transport allowing away fixtures; Increased organisation through the FA, national rules and codification

front: What are some characteristics of elite female footballers in modern-day sport?
back: Equal opportunities making football more available and socially acceptable; Increased media coverage of women's football; More female role models; More clubs being formed; Increased participation through greater funding
group: Changing status of amateur and professionals limited to the development of assossiation football, athletics, lawn tennis

front: What are the socio-cultural factors that have led to football becoming increasingly available to women?
back: Equal opportunities through the Sex Discrimination Act; Women's contribution during the war helped break down myths and stereotypes; Increased media coverage of women's football (e.g. live coverage, EA Sports FIFA 16); More female role models; Greater provision through school PE programmes; Increased approval and encouragement from the FA; More clubs being formed; Increased participation through greater funding; More free time
group: Factors affecting emergance of elite female performers

front: What are some developments in women's football?
back: Increasing prominence across the world; UEFA Women's EURO and UEFA Women's Champions League; Top female footballers becoming personalities and role models; Increased numbers of registered players, qualified referees and coaches; More countries with women's national leagues; Norway, Sweden, Denmark, the Netherlands, Germany, France and England all have 60,000+ female players; Increased earnings and opportunities to play professionally
group: Factors affecting emergance of elite female performers

front: What are some post-WW2 developments in athletics?
back: Interest increased after the 1948 London Olympics; Other countries found ways around strict amateur rules while Britain largely retained them; Trust funds were introduced, allowing athletes to receive financial rewards while maintaining amateur status; The governing body controlled and authorised payments; Day-to-day living expenses were paid, with remaining funds available upon retirement; Athletes could compete worldwide in championships and Grand Prix events, earning appearance fees and prize money
group: Factors affecting emergance of elite female performers

front: What are some characteristics of modern-day athletics?
back: Trust funds are no longer used and athletes can be paid directly within World Athletics (formerly IAAF) rules; World Athletics organises major international competitions with significant prize money; Athletes earn through prize money, sponsorship deals, ticket sales and global media coverage; Women's events have gradually become equal (marathon 1984, triple jump 1996, hammer 2000); Competitions such as the Diamond League allow female athletes to earn millions through their performances
group: Factors affecting emergance of elite female performers
